theme: Unit 6 review, The Mosaic Covenant II, Tabernacle & Holiness
memoryText: For the life of the flesh is in the blood, and I have given it for you on the altar to make atonement for your souls, for it is the blood that makes atonement by the life.
memoryVerseMeditation:
Leviticus 17:11 is the unit’s anchor verse, and it is the clearest explanation in the Old Testament of why sacrifice works the way it does. Read it aloud once more before you continue.

“For the life of the flesh is in the blood.” Blood is not a symbol of death only. It is the sign of life. When an animal’s blood is shed, a life is given up. This is why the sacrifices were solemn. They were not a ritual meal but a taking of life.

“And I have given it for you on the altar.” This is the surprise of the verse. The blood is something God has given. The sacrifice is not the people’s attempt to reach God. It is God’s gift to them. He gives the means by which they may be forgiven. The whole system rests on his initiative.

“To make atonement for your souls.” Atonement is a covering or a ransom. The animal’s life is accepted in place of the worshiper’s. It is the substitute.

“For it is the blood that makes atonement by the life.” The reason it works is that life is given for life. This verse answers the question of why anyone should approach God by blood. It is because the life of the substitute stands in the place of the sinner.

For the Christian, this verse finds its meaning in Jesus. He gave his life, and God gave him for us. “In him we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses” (Ephesians 1:7). “The blood of Jesus his Son cleanses us from all sin” (1 John 1:7).
unitRecap:
In Unit 6 you have read the second half of the book of Exodus and the whole of Leviticus. You began on Mount Sinai with God’s instructions for the tabernacle. You saw the ark and the mercy seat, the table and the lampstand, the altar and the courtyard, and the clothing of the priests. You learned that the purpose of the whole project was stated in a single sentence: “Let them make me a sanctuary, that I may dwell in their midst.”

You saw how quickly the people fell. While Moses was on the mountain, they made a golden calf, and he interceded for them. You heard him ask to see God’s glory, and you heard God proclaim his name: merciful and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in steadfast love and faithfulness. You watched the covenant renewed, the tabernacle built, and the glory of the LORD fill the tent. You prayed through Psalm 15 and Psalm 24, which ask who may stand in God’s presence.

In Leviticus, you studied the five main offerings and what each one teaches about atonement, thanksgiving, and peace. You read how the priests were ordained, and how Nadab and Abihu died when they offered unauthorized fire. You studied the laws of clean and unclean, and you saw how the priest goes outside the camp to welcome the healed person back. The center of the unit was the Day of Atonement, with its blood on the mercy seat and its two goats, and you prayed Psalm 51 as the cry of a broken heart.

You read the Holiness Code and its great command to love your neighbor as yourself. You read the calendar of Israel’s festivals, the Sabbath year, and the Jubilee, and the covenant’s blessings and curses. You ended with the psalms: Psalm 50, which says that God wants thanksgiving more than empty sacrifice, Psalm 40, which speaks of an open ear and a delight in God’s will, Psalm 91, a song of trust in God’s shelter, and Psalm 92, a song for the Sabbath.

The unit taught that God is holy, that sin is costly, that atonement is God’s gift, and that a forgiven people are called to be holy as he is holy.

reviewQuestions.question: What is the Tabernacle teaching us about how sinners can approach a holy God?
reviewQuestions.prompt: Think about the layout of the tent, from the gate to the Most Holy Place. Consider the altar, the basin, the veil, and the priest. Look back at Exodus 25:8 and Hebrews 9:11-12.

reviewQuestions.question: What does the sacrificial system reveal about the nature of atonement?
reviewQuestions.prompt: Review the five offerings in Leviticus 1 to 7. Look at the laying on of hands and the role of blood. Consider Leviticus 17:11 and what it means that God gave the blood.

reviewQuestions.question: What happens on the Day of Atonement, and how does it point to Christ?
reviewQuestions.prompt: Recall the high priest, the mercy seat, and the two goats from Leviticus 16. Read Hebrews 9:24-28 and 10:11-14. Ask what is different about Christ’s sacrifice.

reviewQuestions.question: What does “be holy as I am holy” mean for the people of God?
reviewQuestions.prompt: Look back at Leviticus 19, where holiness includes love for neighbor, honest dealing, and care for the poor. Read 1 Peter 1:13-16. Ask how holiness is both a gift and a calling.

prayerPrompts: Thank God for teaching his people how to come near.
Thank him for Jesus, the blood on the altar for your atonement.
Ask him to keep the unit verse in front of you.
